about: The fixed list of Villacana areas. Every reference photo, map and doc is tagged against these ids, and scripts/build_references.py writes one brief per area in refs/areas/. 'match' auto-tags a phone photo from where the camera stood (street ids from public/map/skeleton.json, pool ids, seafront parts, and a radius in metres round a point). Camera position is only a first guess: a photo's 'shows' tags in data/reference_tags.json override it.

areas.name: North pool
areas.summary: The clover-shaped north pool, its lawn ring, crazy-paving path, curved garden walls and the terraces round it.
notes: Dave (2026-10-11): the lawn is bigger than the first pass showed, and the houses have front porches.
Skip the glass safety fence round the pools (Dave, 2026-10-11).
Best single reference: villacana-reference/photos/07 (whole courtyard looking north).

Issue #36 reconciliation (2026-10-15): north-side patios are 0.25–0.4 m above the path, separate from the NW six-riser 0.9–1.1 m terrace owned by #54. The old five-riser/0.75 m model is withdrawn; issue #36 remains open pending the raised-terraces module and individual north-patio/opening traces. Historical NW coordinate candidates are review-only, with stair placement still conflicting with the survey bearing estimate.

Issue #54 (2026-10-16): the NW six-riser tiled stair is built at about (-189.3, 17.8), cut back into a 1.0 m terrace (data/raised_terraces.json) between the curved wall and a straight wall that runs east to a pier where a path climbs to the north row alley. A camera fit of IMG_2204 to the pool ring puts the stair at bearing 320 from the camera, which IMG_2206 confirms (324); the withdrawn (-181.9, 12) flight would be at 341, so that spot is the pier and alley path, not the stair. Open: the terrace floor stands 0.5-1 m above the model datum of the houses behind it (6165501UF1366N_part5, part1); whether their floors are higher or there are steps down is not visible. The west and south ends of the terrace are estimated.

Issue #36 (2026-10-17): lower northern plinth band, three independent shallow white-nosed openings and visible northwest/north crazy-paving path built separately from #54. The 0.325 m floor is a conservative visible band; rear and side floor limits and hidden patio divisions are untraced estimates, not surveyed property boundaries. Houses, pool and lawn keep their datum.

Issue #95: the circled gap between the west row and standalone house has three separately observed upper balcony canopies, traced from the georeferenced aerial and Apple02/08/09. These structural roofs were missing in Layout; generic optional porches are not a replacement. Roof edges and elevations remain estimated, hidden ground boundaries untraced. The IMG_2206 brown doors are poolward of the marked gap. Current north/whole renders retain turf and deck; the supplied screenshot surface absence remains unreproduced.

Alignment audit 2026-10-18 (docs/reviews/north-pool-alignment-audit): Google screenshot globally registered to fixed Esri frame; held-out relative residuals about 1.5-2.1 m, sampled roof/registry differences about 0.6-1.5 m do not establish ground-wall shifts. No runtime geometry changed. IMG_2202/2361 are the separate private36/34 entry, not IMG_2363 lawn gateway. Missing newer photo-check records do not erase earlier manual reviews. Concealed boundaries, complete pool/ground perimeter and access widths remain unresolved in north-pool-unresolved-plan.

areas.name: Middle pool
areas.summary: The clover-shaped middle pool courtyard, entered through arched white gateways off tiled lanes.
notes: Lanes are square terracotta tiles with a pebble border; the courtyard is entered through arched white gateways with black iron gates.
Skip the glass safety fence round the pools (Dave, 2026-10-11).

IMG_2340 (outside) and IMG_2244 (inside) show the east gateway from Calle Eva: white piers, curved coping, black iron gate, Comunidad Villacana notice. IMG_2332 shows a raised white planter wall (about 0.8 m) with a hedge along the west path.

IMG_2333: three stone steps climb a tiled path to a gate on the south-west side. IMG_2334: black iron double gate under a curved pergola frame on the south side, raised planter beside it. IMG_2335: blue tile panel on a raised planter. IMG_2331 (±17 m) and IMG_2341 (±47 m) have poor GPS.

Built 2026-10-14 (docs/MIDDLE_POOL.md): the east gateway from Calle Eva (piers, flat head, curved coping, open iron leaf, notices) and the raised west planter with its hedge, which turns the south-west corner beside the IMG_2333 steps.

Issue #39: separate level south entrance from IMG_2334/2335: two open iron leaves, shallow curved white head with metal pergola ribs, crazy paving and flush drain, raised white planter flanking an inset step and a schematic blue/yellow border round a white tile panel. Placed across Calle Silvia near its courtyard end; positions/ends (about 1–2 m) and dimensions are estimates. No south-lane grade change is inferred; the southwest steps and western 0.5 m rise remain separate.

Issue 48 source pass: a bounded curved north planter termination, three white side steps, short brown-door wall and open pergola are modelled from IMG_2331/2332/2195; exact extents and dimensions remain estimates. IMG_2331/2332 cameras are corrected independently from aerial path/pool anchors, original GPS retained. Browser and matched-camera review pending; south-west steps/gateway and south gate are separate tasks.

Issue 48 follows the existing continuous western +0.5 m terrain rise for the north steps, using tread-minus-siteY offsets in the shared ramp-steps module; no additional isolated plateau. Pool, deck and west path remain at 0 m. Flight dimensions and bounded wall extents remain estimated pending browser/image review.

Issue #31 (PRs #53 and #60): IMG_2333 shows three rough stone risers on the planter side of Calle Eva, a tiled ramp beside them, a short landing and a white gateway with two open iron leaves. The steps and the 0.5 m rise to the Dalí level are in data/middle_pool_steps.json and data/terrain.json; the gateway is in data/middle_pool_sw_gateway.json. Positions and sizes are estimated from tiles.

Issue #55: bounded north patio floor at +0.45 m behind a +0.8 m white wall (IMG_2193/2194); stops before the photographed grass opening, with no inferred stairs. Shallow oleander bed at +0.2 m from IMG_2246/2247. Only a short +0.4 m curved hedge-wall fragment is estimated from IMG_2341: its GPS is ±47 m and its north-east placement remains uncertain. Floor extents, wall ends and all heights are low-confidence estimates; no hidden private boundaries or gates are traced. See docs/MIDDLE_POOL_RAISED_PATIOS.md.

18 October (Dave's review of the live site): the south gate's tiled wall bench was built behind the open right leaf. IMG_2334 read by perspective puts it about 1.7-2.7 m in from the gate past about 1.7 m of planter; it is now seat height with a plinth. IMG_2334/2335 pins were corrected from photo content. Open: the forecourt inside the gate is crazy paving with a hedge, not lawn (task middle-pool-south-forecourt).

21 October draft (middle-pool-south-forecourt): bounded 5.15 × 2.12 m crazy-paving patch replaces the crossing tile render locally, with a Details-only east hedge fragment. Gate, bench/planter, registry footprints, route axes, terrain and collision retained. Photos confirm material/side ordering, not the estimated endpoints. Aerial shade/foliage conceal full edges; Eva crossing still interrupts the photographed hedge/corridor. Independent source review withholds full placement approval; task stays in progress. See docs/reviews/middle-pool-south-forecourt/.

21 October user clarification: two planted house-frontage strips are visible along the tiled lane beyond IMG_2334 gate. Left has a low kerb/mixed plants; right has raised white bed sections and an open recessed doorway between them. These are distinct from the courtyard hedge/bench. Source-relative photo/plan mapping is in docs/reviews/middle-pool-south-forecourt/lane-planters/. No global dimensions inferred: IMG_2189 is not a securely established reverse view of this curved double gate. The window bars identified by the user are projecting black grilles above the planted border (clear on photo-right in IMG_2334); IMG_2189 supplies clearer bowed grille examples on both sides as appearance evidence only.

22 October reference-pack pilot: numbered photo locators/traces and 41 component rows keep gate view, lane detail, Silvia1–15 passage and Jorge27–35 passage distinct. Silvia tunnel arch/flat ceiling/walls/doors/exit are not accounted for by the existing floor citation; precise connection and owner target remain unresolved. No geometry changed. See docs/REFERENCE_PACK_WORKFLOW.md and public/reference-packs/entrance/index.html.

23 October entrance context: user questions gate/bench/planter distance from pool. Satellite and IMG_2192 confirm lawn/hedged approach buffer, but ground anchors are concealed, so gate, bench, pool and tunnel transform are retained. Bounded PR108 street-side planters, square window cages and four-course paving are transplanted into the main scene; bench cypress/geranium-like planting and small pale cabinet added from2334/2335/2192. Extents and facade attachments remain estimates, with shared route-clearance guard and open discrepancy. See docs/reviews/tunnel-entrance-context/.

24 October planter correction: a bounded low right garden bed, left greenery with its base unresolved, and continuing near path beyond the Silvia exit arch replace two unsupported illustrative tall garden pots; four observed near/threshold pots remain. At the pool entrance the existing bench beds gain rounded returns/white rims/soil inside their original bounds, and a short LOW grey-beige kerb follows the existing opposite hedge fragment. Satellite context/full photos independently rechecked; no measured extent, complete garden perimeter, route/gate/pool relocation or placement approval is inferred. See docs/reviews/silvia-entrance-planters/.

areas.name: South pool
areas.summary: The clover-shaped south pool, its lawn, the date palm and the low seaward wall.
notes: IMG_2349 and IMG_2188: the south lawn and level pool stand about 1 m above the paseo behind the sandstone wall and mesh fence. Existing paseo profile supplies that difference; south pool stays at datum 0. The legacy seaward white wall is omitted wherever sandstone replaces it in map, 3D and collision. Short end returns remain approximate, not photographed endpoints.

areas.name: Main pool
areas.summary: The large main pool, the round toddler pool, the deck and lawn, Bistro Enrique's and its steps, 90 Miles.
notes: Villacana has one large main pool with a round toddler pool beside it (Dave, 2026-10-11).

Apple 3D screenshots (Dave, 2026-10-21, apple-maps/10-13): Calle Guillermo runs down beside the lawn to the paseo, the kiosk at its foot is at lawn level, and the east steps are a narrow flight from the Picasso wall between the 90 Miles terrace and the east building. Built by task guillermo-slope-east-steps (docs/MAIN_POOL.md); heights estimated.

Dave, 2026-10-21: a fence and a coastal gate separate Villacana from Barraka beach in front of the lawn. IMG_2226 shows the white wall, a round-arched gateway at the foot of Calle Guillermo, a short wall and white railings along the lawn; built as data/seafront_fence.json (heights by eye, gateway left open).

Dave, 2026-10-21: Calle Jorge meets Guillermo on the level; Guillermo's ramp starts just past the junction and slopes down to the paseo as a smooth ramp with no steps (modelled 3 m over 15.5 m, about 19 %). Open: do the houses beside the ramp stand lower than street level?

areas.name: Calle Elena
areas.summary: Calle Elena, north and south sections, from the north pool to the middle pool, including the ramp and steps at its junction with Cervantes.
notes: IMG_2254 shows the sign CALLE ELENA 18-30.

Built 2026-10-14 (docs/ELENA_NORTH.md): arched gateway to the north pool lawn, east patio wall, west planting strip, magnolia bed, two hedged beds with pollarded trees, two planter boxes, and the three steps beside the Cervantes ramp.
The Cervantes/Elena rise is 0.5 m over about 3 m (steps beside a ramp, IMG_2286), not 7 m.
Not modelled yet: the east-side patios beyond the beds.
IMG_2286 GPS is ±14 m: do not place geometry from its pin alone.

IMG_2355 and IMG_2328 (14 Oct) confirm the three steps beside the Cervantes ramp and the drain across the whole lane. Roof shots IMG_2358, 2366, 2367 look down on the junction lawns and the east-side patios.

Issue #34: the short paved spur between the two hedged beds now reaches a closed timber door in a finite white garden wall; the barred window is in a short transverse return at the north end of the planted bed (IMG_2199-2201). Extents against existing bed backs and heights are estimated; no unseen patio enclosure or level change is inferred.
Not modelled yet: the garden door between the hedged beds, the east-side patios beyond the beds.

Issue #46: the first paired iron gateway and short patterned tiled entry west of covered walkway 6265201UF1366N_part5 are modelled from IMG_2361/2202; IMG_2203 faces the opposite open end. Gates enclose a private side entry beyond the passage, leaving the complete covered walkway open. Gateway dimensions and placement remain estimates; further gates/enclosures in the roof view are untraced.

Issue #38 (docs/ELENA_EAST_PATIOS.md): the roof shots IMG_2366/IMG_2360 look along Cervantes east of the junction (the trained-trunk wall, curved-coping door and cane-roofed pergola are on the Cervantes south side, cf. IMG_2197; new task cervantes-east-south-patios). The patios behind the Elena garden wall are hidden under the magnolia canopy from every roof camera, so their partitions, floors and levels stay unmodelled. Built from ground photos: the garden wall continued behind the second hedged bed (IMG_2197, IMG_2199), a solid white wall behind the plumbago bed closing the patios off from Cervantes (IMG_2356), and a timber pergola behind the garden door (IMG_2199, IMG_2200); extents and heights estimated.

Issue #57 (data/door_sills.json): red-tread sills, 0.12 m, at the two brown doors in the white wall west of the junction lawns (IMG_2260/2261/2330). Not modelled yet: that wall and its doors. The door on the east side at the junction (IMG_2253) has no visible sill and was left out. Open: the terrain rule's guessed west rise puts these lawns 0.2-0.3 m above the lane, while the photos show them level with it behind a 0.1 m kerb.

areas.name: Calle Miguel de Cervantes
areas.summary: Cervantes, the straight tiled lane across the block from Pintor Dalí to the Picasso car-park access, its ramp, patio walls and covered passages.
notes: Straight narrow lane, square terracotta tiles, window grilles, lantern brackets; a drain and sloping exit onto Dalí (IMG_2273–2275).
At Elena the lane is split: smooth ramp on the south half, three steps on the north half, built 2026-10-14 (docs/ELENA_NORTH.md). The rise there is 0.5 m over about 3 m.
IMG_2288 shows CALLE MIGUEL inside a passage; reading it as Miguel de Cervantes is interpretation.
IMG_2327: two red-tread steps up to a door just west of the Elena junction. IMG_2356: plumbago hedge and white kerb wall on Cervantes east of Elena.

IMG_2368/2369/2359: three partial transverse patio partitions north of Cervantes traced with Details-only climbers/shrubs (docs/CERVANTES_NORTH_PATIOS.md). Concealed joins and complete enclosure boundaries remain unasserted; plan endpoints estimated to about 1–2 m.

IMG_2356 north-side white plumbago kerb built as a bounded 8 m test east of Elena (issue #43). Wall/hedge relationship photo-supported; exact extent, height and alignment estimated. IMG_2360 gives roof context, not a measured boundary. Further eastern frontage remains unasserted.

Issue #33 review (2026-10-15): IMG_2327/2328 show two door steps immediately downhill of the ramp drain, distinct from the three ramp steps. Historical blocker (resolved by the later garden-wall survey): the nearest modeled north solid facade is 6.17 m from the drain and the roof/aerial views do not uniquely locate this doorway. The assumed house-facade requirement was incorrect; see docs/CERVANTES_DOOR_STEPS_REVIEW.md.

Issue #33 implementation after the levels survey: the brown door is in a garden wall at the lane edge, not the house facade, resolving the historical 6.17 m blocker. A closed door with curved coping, two .225 m red-tread steps, bounded private patio at +.45 m and west bed at +.425 m are modeled; full patio extent and position remain estimated. Browser/camera acceptance pending.

2026-10-15 (#45): IMG_2329/2342 show the same near-corner pollarded lawn tree; IMG_2358/2367 and IMG_2260 show three clipped trees in sequence beside the lane, two in the nearer lawn and one beyond the door approach. Details positions/heights estimated; the existing lawn/white-kerb rings remain approximate because the oblique roof views do not calibrate their metric extents.

Issue #56 (2026-10-16): IMG_2286/2355/2328 count each Elena step tread as one 0.4 m tile plus a grey stone nosing; risers moved to 0.4, 0.92 and 1.45 m from the drain, 3 m ramp run kept, every tread above the ramp beside it.

Issue #89 (2026-10-17): roof IMG_2366/2360 and ground IMG_2197 support the white lane-side south patio wall east of Elena, closed curved-coping brown door and cane-roofed timber pergola against 6265601UF1366N_part1. One bounded 18.2 m frontage, door and pergola built; no internal partitions or concealed enclosure returns asserted. Aerial/registry context checked; endpoints and dimensions remain estimated at roughly 1–2 m. Roof-camera diagnostic uses estimated 7.2 m local eye elevation and within-uncertainty roof-edge camera correction, not a calibrated match.

areas.name: Calle Pintor Dalí
areas.summary: Pintor Dalí, its car park and bays, the outer chain-link fence, the seaward turning area and the coastal gate to the paseo.
notes: The seaward boundary has a narrow pedestrian gate (IMG_2284, 2296, 2297): never close it off with a continuous fence.
IMG_2280 is a flagstone pedestrian entrance, distinct from Cervantes' square tiles; no readable street sign.

Issue #57 (data/door_sills.json): the house-side footpath and grass strip between Eva and Patricia stand a 0.12 m white kerb above the asphalt (IMG_2291-2293), with a slot drain at the arched porch; the lawn strip ends about 17 m along and cars nose up to the path beyond it. The south flagstone approach rises 0.25 m over 5 m to the arch in 6263501UF1366S_part1 between flared kerbs (IMG_2283/2294/2295); the passage behind the arch is not opened. Open: the map puts Calle Patricia about 3.7 m south of the photographed apron kerb.

areas.name: Pintor Picasso and the car park
areas.summary: Calle Pintor Picasso, the inner car-park access aisle and the Picasso car park.
notes: IMG_2345 supports bounded utility fronts/brown doors, boundary wall, stone plinth/railings, short ramp and Details-only bins. Frontage offsets and dimensions remain estimated at the existing Picasso road; registry houses, asphalt route and site levels are retained. Ramp is solid inaccessible private-frontage geometry; no new walkable elevated platform or unseen wall continuation is asserted.

areas.name: Loira, Bolivia, Alberto and Isabel
areas.summary: The northern boundary roads and the lanes round the north pool's upper side.

areas.name: Calle Eva
areas.summary: Calle Eva round the middle pool, and its west-side footpath to Patricia.
notes: IMG_2339: walled lawn corners with bougainvillea trained flat along the walls and green bollard lights.

Calle Eva ends at the middle pool east gateway (built 2026-10-14, docs/MIDDLE_POOL.md), level with the corner of the house on its south-east side; the lawn wall north-west of it steps down to about 1.45 m.

IMG_2339 corner reuses the unchanged middle gateway NW wing and adds only a 4.2 m return, with a bounded lawn. Two wall-aligned single planes replace the crossed bougainvillea there; bollard, clipped hedge, nearby rounded tree and lantern are Details-only and route guarded. Lengths, heights and adjacent lawn extent remain estimates; no surveyed enclosure closure or new level change is asserted.

areas.name: Patricia, Silvia, Jorge, Teodoro Rojo and Guillermo
areas.summary: The lanes between the middle pool and the beach.
notes: IMG_2235/2237/2239 support octagonal terracotta with diamond infills on the photographed Teodoro Rojo run; IMG_2240 remains square. IMG_2185/2190 support cream/blue corner inserts in covered-floor tiles. Material masks use existing ground/registry strips; tile dimensions and passage extents remain estimates, and solid registry strips may still obscure the floor until separately traced as passages. No levels or geometry were changed.

22 October reference-pack pilot: numbered photo locators/traces and 41 component rows keep gate view, lane detail, Silvia1–15 passage and Jorge27–35 passage distinct. Silvia tunnel arch/flat ceiling/walls/doors/exit are not accounted for by the existing floor citation; precise connection and owner target remain unresolved. No geometry changed. See docs/REFERENCE_PACK_WORKFLOW.md and public/reference-packs/entrance/index.html.

Owner clarification: the narrow side spaces in the Silvia tunnel are recessed entrances with brown doors. Photo-relative 3D study includes the two visible paired doors plus two owner-confirmed inner entrances with guessed 0.65 m recesses and generic wooden doors; inventory now has T13/T14 (43 total). Study has no global map transform; connection and measured placement remain unresolved.

Owner correction to the Silvia tunnel study: the two inner recessed entrance doors are plain single brown wooden leaves with round gold knobs. This clarifies hidden door styling, while recess depth and world placement remain estimates.

Owner clarification applies to all tunnel entrance doors, including the nearer bays: use normal-width single brown leaves with one round gold knob each. Earlier paired-door readings remain source history, superseded for the model. Recess footprints and world-registration uncertainty are unchanged.

23 October main-map integration draft reuses the corrected Silvia model at an approximate west-side registry-topology candidate: canopy 6264401UF1366S_part2, lower corridor through part3 to its courtyard, preserving upper floor/roof. Map and Walk/collision share one transform. Photo heading conflicts and opposite-side host remain unresolved; no measured placement approval. See docs/reviews/silvia-main-integration/.

24 October planter correction: a bounded low right garden bed, left greenery with its base unresolved, and continuing near path beyond the Silvia exit arch replace two unsupported illustrative tall garden pots; four observed near/threshold pots remain. At the pool entrance the existing bench beds gain rounded returns/white rims/soil inside their original bounds, and a short LOW grey-beige kerb follows the existing opposite hedge fragment. Satellite context/full photos independently rechecked; no measured extent, complete garden perimeter, route/gate/pool relocation or placement approval is inferred. See docs/reviews/silvia-entrance-planters/.

24 October Silvia paving correction: full2190/2191 floor reinspection identifies square terracotta units offset around small blue/cream squares, creating diagonal insert runs. Earlier clipped-corner description was imprecise. Current surface uses coherent metric UVs, varied aged tiles/grout/motifs and wall pebble bands; precise pitches/angle remain estimates. Existing floor extents, topology, level, collision and tunnel/bed positions retained. See docs/reviews/silvia-paving/.

areas.name: Barraka and the beach
areas.summary: The beach in front of Villacana, the Barraka beach restaurant and the sea.
notes: The beach is mixed sand, stones and rounded pebbles, not uniform pale sand (IMG_2300).
IMG_2346, IMG_2347: BARRAKA BEACH painted planter, thatched parasols and a timber boardwalk across the sand.

IMG_2346/2347 show narrow weathered green timber access, a white two-tier planted BARRAKA BEACH sign on its left looking seaward, and straw parasols. Added as ground-following planks plus guarded Details furniture; dimensions and seasonal furniture positions are estimates. IMG_2225 wooden cream-cushion beds differ from the blue/white plastic loungers west of the aisle in IMG_2223; those are not asserted as one type. No coast, paseo or registry footprint changes.

Issue #32: the existing georeferenced Esri aerial independently places the wet shoreline band seaward of the old OSM coast by up to about 30 m near Barraka. data/shoreline_trace.json records pixel control points; the local beach/sea edge now shares that trace. IMG_2285 is about 16.5 m inland of it, without changing its GPS. Estimated 3–5 m trace/registration precision; acquisition date, tide and seasonal changes remain unknown.

2026-10-19 owner clarification and independent original-photo/map review: green aisle is immediately left/northeast of actual Barraka restaurant 6364501UF1366S_part8 looking towards the sea. The planter, separate log-filled cooking boat and thatched cooking shelter are all left of this aisle; boat beyond planter. The old southwest run [30,121] to [42,135] used the wrong flank. Proposed corrected axis [31,101] to [43,115] and planter [36,102] remain estimates, not <=2m approved measurements; precise hut/boat footprints remain unresolved. See docs/reviews/barraka-planter-placement.

The old 25m GPS conflict was computed against the wrong southwest aisle and is retracted as evidence of a camera error. Raw pins remain unchanged; IMG_2347 lies roughly 6.5m from the tentative NE-axis landward end. Registry parts6465801UF1366N_part5/part6 remain non-standing dashed outlines; their photo citations legitimately support absence of a building, not cooking-hut identity.

areas.name: The paseo
areas.summary: The seafront promenade between the resort's seaward walls and the beach.
notes: IMG_2350: the paseo is pink stamped concrete with a timber edge onto the beach; a yellow sandstone retaining wall with a green mesh fence on top holds the seafront houses above it. Built 14 October (data/paseo_wall.json, docs/SEAFRONT.md): about 134 m from the Dalí apron to the end of Calle Guillermo, about 1 m high by the south lawn (the paseo there was lowered from street level to match), lower towards Dalí.

Open: towards its east end the model makes the wall up to 3 m (the paseo falls to big-pool level there), but IMG_2227 from the beach suggests it stays about 1 m. A photo from the paseo near Calle Guillermo would settle it.
IMG_2349, IMG_2352 and IMG_2354 show the same sandstone retaining wall and green mesh fence running along the paseo, including right below the south pool (IMG_2349).

Issue #35: paseo centreline generated 1.5 m seaward of the aerial/photo-backed sandstone wall, 3 m approximate width; pavement now meets the face as IMG_2350/IMG_2352/IMG_2354 show. Southwest former hold-in removed against aerial; gate approach and Barraka boardwalk OSM joins retained. Plan accuracy about 1-2 m, not a survey. Eastern wall height (#40) and registry house obstruction (#41) remain unresolved; levels and footprints unchanged.

Issue #40 evidence review (15 October): IMG_2227/IMG_2226 from the beach and IMG_2350 looking east do not resolve whether the paseo rises or the gardens fall near Guillermo. The nominal 3 m east-end wall is a result of the approximate paseo profile against assumed inland ground, not a measured height. All levels retained, including Dave's main-pool drop; task remains open. See docs/PASEO_EAST_END_HEIGHT_REVIEW.md for the specific photo needed.

Issue #49: Details-only bounded clipped hedges behind mesh (IMG_2349/2352/2354), short green cloth runs (IMG_2350/2352), four photographed slim white lamps on the paving at the wall foot and a flush service-cover surface (IMG_2354). Positions/dimensions estimated relative to shared wall, not GPS subjects. Along the wall run the protected route is the 2.2 m clear walk beyond the lamps (paving stays 3 m), so all four lamps stand where the photos show them; lamp count/spacing beyond the photographed run is not invented.

Issue #41 (16 October): after PR #64 the eastern OSM paseo still entered registry part 6465801UF1366N_part5 by 2.8 m (and part6 by 0.5 m), not 0.64 m from it. On the aerial the pink paseo (about 3.5 m wide) crosses both parts and the rest of part5 is open sand; neighbouring registry roofs match the image, and IMG_2346/IMG_2347 (pins about 4 m) show sand, the Barraka sign planter and a walkway there. So the footprint, not the line, was wrong: both parts keep their exact rings as dashed registry outlines with floors 0 (data/registry_corrections.json), no longer extruded or solid. Paseo points unchanged; the whole paseo now keeps 1.5 m from every standing house and is walked end to end both ways. Open: east of Barraka the OSM line runs along the landward edge of the pink strip, about 2 m landward of its centre on the aerial.

Dave, 2026-10-21, on a render of the corner by Calle Guillermo: the sandstone wall is not 3 m tall there. The garden behind its east end now falls to 1 m above the paseo (data/main_pool.json gardenFall), so the wall stays about 1 m (task guillermo-slope-east-steps); this answers issue #40's question in favour of the gardens falling. The fall's shape is estimated.

areas.name: The whole resort
areas.summary: Overviews, maps and wide views covering several areas at once, and the mountain backdrop.
notes: Buildings are white with brown wooden Persian-blind shutters (Dave, 2026-10-11).
Plants and small details should eventually be textures and sprites, not 3D shapes. The player should be able to get into the pools.
GPS locates the camera, not the subject. A roof or upper-floor photo's pin is inside a building and its subject can be 50+ m away.
